source_refs.note: Book p. 5: 1.3.2 Non-Fundamental Transcendental Functions, examples, Examples 5 and 6

blocks.text: Pichle subtopic mein humne buniyadi blocks (fundamental transcendental functions) dekhe. Ab dekhte hain ke jab in blocks ko jora jaye, ya ek ko doosre ke andar daala jaye, to kya banta hai. Isi ko non-fundamental transcendental function kehte hain.

Kitab ki definition: jo functions transcendental functions ko algebraic functions ke saath jor kar (combine kar ke), ya transformations aur composition (ek function ko doosre ke andar daalna) laga kar bante hain, woh non-fundamental transcendental functions hain.

Is definition mein teen mushkil lafz hain, pehle unhein aasan kar lein. Combining (jorna) ka matlab hai do functions ko jama, tafreeq, zarb ya taqseem karna, jaise \(\sin x + \ln x\). Transformation (shakal ya jagah badalna) ka matlab hai graph ko khiskana, phailana ya sukerna, jaise \(\ln x\) ki jagah \(\ln x + 3\). Composition (ek function ke andar doosra function) ka matlab hai ke ek function ka output doosre ka input ban jaye, jaise \(e^{x^{2}}\) mein pehle \(x^{2}\) banta hai aur phir woh \(e\) ki power mein jata hai. In teeno mein se koi bhi kaam ho jaye to function buniyadi block nahin rehta.

Kitab ki misalein: \(y = \sin x + \ln x\), \(y = e^{x^{2}}\), \(y = x \sin x\), \(y = \ln 2x\) aise functions hain jo fundamental transcendental functions nahin. Doosri taraf \(y = 10^{2x}\) ek standard transcendental function hai, kyun ke ise \(y = 100^{x}\) likha ja sakta hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan "standard transcental function" likhti hai; sahi lafz "transcendental" hai. Matlab \(y = 10^{2x}\) ek standard (fundamental) transcendental function hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sawal yeh hai ke \(10^{2x}\) fundamental kyun hai jab ke \(e^{x^{2}}\) nahin? Is ke liye indices ka qanoon \((a^{m})^{n} = a^{mn}\) yaad kijiye:
\[10^{2x} = (10^{2})^{x} = 100^{x}\]
Yeh bilkul \(a^{x}\) wali shakal hai, \(a = 100\) ke saath. Yani bhes badla hua tha, asal mein yeh standard block hi tha. Lekin \(e^{x^{2}}\) ko kisi constant \(a\) ke saath \(a^{x}\) nahin likha ja sakta, kyun ke is ka exponent \(x^{2}\) hai, \(x\) ka constant multiple nahin. Yeh \(e^{u}\) aur \(u = x^{2}\) ka composition hai.
Har misaal kaise bani: \(\sin x + \ln x\) (do standard functions ka jor), \(x \sin x\) (algebraic function \(x\) ke saath zarb), \(e^{x^{2}}\) (composition), \(\ln 2x\) (\(2x\) ke saath composition; yeh \(\ln x\) ka transformation bhi hai kyun ke \(x > 0\) ke liye \(\ln 2x = \ln 2 + \ln x\), yani graph bas \(\ln 2\) upar khisak jata hai).

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: "Non-fundamental" likhne se pehle hamesha koshish karein ke function ko ek standard function ki shakal mein likh sakein. Maslan \(4^{x/2} = (4^{1/2})^{x} = 2^{x}\), to yeh fundamental hai. Agar dobara likhna kaam na kare, to jawab mein izafi operation ka naam likhein (sum, product, composition ya jama kiya hua constant). Is se examiner ko pata chalta hai ke aap ne wajah samajh kar jawab diya hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Ek aasan sa test: neeche har function ke baare mein socho ke kya yeh akela standard block hai? \(\cos x\), \(\cos x + 5\), \(7^{x}\), \(\ln(x^{2} + 1)\).
Jawab: \(\cos x\) aur \(7^{x}\) akele standard blocks hain, is liye fundamental. \(\cos x + 5\) mein constant jama hua (combination), aur \(\ln(x^{2} + 1)\) mein \(\ln\) ke andar \(x\) ki jagah \(x^{2} + 1\) hai (composition), is liye dono non-fundamental hain. Dekha aap ne? Sawal hamesha yahi hai: kya block akela hai, ya us ke saath kuch aur bhi kiya gaya hai?
Ab kitab ki do misalein dekhte hain. Pehli misaal mein sawal hai "algebraic ya transcendental?", aur doosri mein "fundamental ya non-fundamental?". Dono mein farq ghaur se dekhiye.

blocks.title: Example 5
blocks.problem:
Given the following functions:
\(f(x) = \sqrt{x+1}\), \(g(x) = e^{x}\), \(h(x) = \frac{x+1}{x^{2}-2x+1}\), \(q(x) = \ln 2x\), \(r(x) = \sin x\).
Classify each function as algebraic or transcendental.
steps:
Diya gaya: paanch functions \(f, g, h, q, r\).
Maloom karna: in mein kaun algebraic hai aur kaun transcendental.
Tareeqa: sab se pehle rule yaad kijiye. Function algebraic hai agar woh \(x\) se sirf mehdood \(+, -, \times, \div\) aur roots se bane (tab woh \(y\) ki polynomial equation satisfy karta hai). Agar \(x\) kisi exponential, logarithmic ya trigonometric function ke andar ho, to function transcendental hai. Plan: ek ek function ko utha kar yeh test lagayenge.

Step 1: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x+1}\)
\[y = \sqrt{x+1}\]
\[y^{2} - (x + 1) = 0\]
Kyun: is mein sirf jama aur square root use hua hai. Dono taraf square lene se root khatam ho gaya aur \(y\) ki polynomial equation mil gayi. Is liye \(f\) algebraic hai.
Dhyan dein: root dekh kar ghabrana nahin; root lena algebraic operation hai.

Step 2: \(h(x) = \frac{x+1}{x^{2}-2x+1}\)
\[(x^{2} - 2x + 1)\,y - (x + 1) = 0\]
Kyun: \(h\) do polynomials ki taqseem hai (rational function). Denominator se zarb dene par fraction khatam aur polynomial equation haazir. Is liye \(h\) algebraic hai. Saath mein yeh bhi note karein ke \(x^{2} - 2x + 1 = (x - 1)^{2}\), is liye \(h\) sirf \(x \ne 1\) par defined hai.

Step 3: \(g(x) = e^{x}\)
Kyun: yahan variable \(x\) exponent (power) mein baitha hai; \(e^{x}\) natural exponential function hai. Is liye \(g\) transcendental hai.

Step 4: \(q(x) = \ln 2x\)
Kyun: \(x\) logarithm ke andar hai. Logarithm algebraic operations mein shamil nahin, is liye \(q\) transcendental hai.

Step 5: \(r(x) = \sin x\)
Kyun: \(x\) trigonometric function \(\sin\) ke andar hai. Is liye \(r\) transcendental hai.

Tasdeeq: Step 1 aur 2 wali equations mein function wapas rakh kar dekhte hain:
\[(\sqrt{x+1})^{2} - (x+1) = 0\]
\[(x^{2}-2x+1)\cdot\dfrac{x+1}{x^{2}-2x+1} - (x+1) = 0\]
Dono sahi nikleen, yani \(f\) aur \(h\) waqai algebraic hain. Ginti bhi poori: 2 algebraic + 3 transcendental = 5 functions.
blocks.answer: Algebraic functions: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x+1}\), \(h(x) = \frac{x+1}{x^{2}-2x+1}\). Transcendental functions: \(g(x) = e^{x}\), \(q(x) = \ln 2x\), \(r(x) = \sin x\).

blocks.text: Ek baat ghaur karne wali hai: Example 6 ke paanchon functions transcendental hain, is liye wahan "algebraic" ka sawal hi nahin. Pehle family pehchaanein (algebraic ya transcendental), phir agar transcendental ho to andar ki class (fundamental ya non-fundamental). Yeh do manzil wala faisla hai, bilkul jaise pehle shehar ka naam aur phir mohalle ka naam batate hain.

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem:
Given the following functions:
\(f(x) = \cos 2x + 1\), \(g(x) = 3^{x}\), \(h(x) = \tan^{-1} x^{2}\), \(q(x) = \ln x + e^{x}\), \(r(x) = \tan x\).
Classify each function as fundamental or non-fundamental transcendental functions.
steps:
Diya gaya: paanch transcendental functions \(f, g, h, q, r\).
Maloom karna: kaun fundamental hai aur kaun non-fundamental.
Tareeqa: function fundamental hai agar woh bilkul ek standard function ho (\(a^{x}\), \(\ln x\), ya \(x\) ka koi trigonometric ya inverse trigonometric function), ya dobara likh kar aisa ban jaye. Agar functions ko jora gaya ho, andar \(x\) ki jagah koi aur expression ho, ya constant jama kiya gaya ho, to woh non-fundamental hai. Plan: har function ke saath yeh sawal poochenge: "kya yeh akela standard block hai, ya blocks ko jor kar bana hai?"

Step 1: \(g(x) = 3^{x}\)
\[g(x) = a^{x},\quad a = 3\]
Kyun: yeh seedha standard exponential form hai, aur \(a = 3 > 0\), \(a \ne 1\). Koi izafi operation nahin. Is liye \(g\) fundamental hai.

Step 2: \(r(x) = \tan x\)
Kyun: \(\tan x\) khud \(x\) ka ek standard trigonometric function hai; na kuch jama hua na andar kuch daala gaya. Is liye \(r\) fundamental hai.

Step 3: \(f(x) = \cos 2x + 1\)
Kyun: yahan do kaam hue hain. Pehle standard function \(\cos\) ko \(x\) ki bajaye \(2x\) par lagaya gaya (algebraic function \(2x\) ke saath composition), phir 1 jama kiya gaya (algebraic function ke saath combination). Is liye \(f\) non-fundamental hai.

Step 4: \(h(x) = \tan^{-1}(x^{2})\)
Kyun: standard function \(\tan^{-1}\) ko \(x\) par nahin balke \(x^{2}\) par lagaya gaya hai; yeh composition hai. Is liye \(h\) non-fundamental hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\tan^{-1} x^{2}\) ka matlab \(\tan^{-1}(x^{2})\) hai, \((\tan^{-1} x)^{2}\) nahin.

Step 5: \(q(x) = \ln x + e^{x}\)
Kyun: yeh do mukhtalif standard functions ka jor (sum) hai, yani combination. Is liye \(q\) non-fundamental hai.

Tasdeeq: har fundamental jawab standard families ki ek row se bilkul milta hai (exponential \(a^{x}\); trigonometric \(\tan x\)). Har non-fundamental jawab mein ek izafi kaam hai (\(+1\), andar \(2x\), andar \(x^{2}\), ya sum) jo kisi akele standard function mein nahin hota. Ginti: 2 fundamental + 3 non-fundamental = 5.
blocks.answer: Fundamental transcendental functions: \(g(x) = 3^{x}\), \(r(x) = \tan x\). Non-fundamental transcendental functions: \(f(x) = \cos 2x + 1\), \(h(x) = \tan^{-1}(x^{2})\), \(q(x) = \ln x + e^{x}\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(y = 2^{3x}\) aur \(y = x^{2} e^{x}\) ko classify kijiye.
Jawab: \(2^{3x} = (2^{3})^{x} = 8^{x}\), to yeh fundamental hai. \(x^{2} e^{x}\) mein algebraic function \(x^{2}\) ko \(e^{x}\) se zarb diya gaya hai, is liye yeh non-fundamental hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Non-fundamental transcendental functions standard functions se bante hain: algebraic functions ke saath jor ya zarb, transformation, ya composition se.
2. Jo function ek standard shakal mein dobara likha ja sake woh fundamental hai: \(10^{2x} = 100^{x}\).
3. Example 5 mein sawal "algebraic ya transcendental" tha, aur Example 6 mein "fundamental ya non-fundamental". Pehle sawal ko ghaur se parhiye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(10^{2x}\) ko sirf \(2x\) dekh kar non-fundamental keh dena. Pehle dobara likhiye: \(10^{2x} = 100^{x}\).
2. \(e^{x^{2}}\) ko fundamental samajhna. Yaad rakhiye \(e^{x^{2}} \ne (e^{x})^{2} = e^{2x}\); is ka exponent \(x^{2}\) hai, is liye yeh composition hai.
3. \(\tan^{-1} x^{2}\) mein bracket bhool jana. Is ka matlab \(\tan^{-1}(x^{2})\) hai, \((\tan^{-1} x)^{2}\) nahin.
